title: Scheduling
hook: One CPU core runs one thing at a time — the scheduler rapidly switches so everyone gets a turn.

steps.caption: A runs for a time slice, then the scheduler pauses it.

nodeCaptions.cpu: Hardware executes whoever is currently scheduled.
nodeCaptions.a: State is saved so A can resume later.

steps.caption: B gets the core next — A isn’t finished, just waiting its turn.

nodeCaptions.b: Fairness vs throughput vs latency — policies differ.

steps.caption: C runs, then maybe A again. Nobody needs to finish first for others to make progress.

nodeCaptions.c: Preemption is why your UI can stay responsive while something compiles.

takeaways: Scheduling multiplexes one core across many runnable tasks.
Time slices + saved state create the illusion of simultaneity.
Policy choices change what feels “fair” or “laggy.”

quiz.question: If three processes are runnable on one core, what does the scheduler do?
choices: Runs all three machine instructions in true parallel on that core
Switches the core between them over time
quiz.explanation: One core, one thread of execution at a time — switching creates concurrency.
